analyst_view.overall: Leeds are 7th and in good form, having beaten Tottenham 1-0 and then won 4-1 at Chelsea on 21 November, with Noah Okafor and Dominic Calvert-Lewin both fit and scoring. Promoted Coventry are 14th, three points above the drop zone, after a 3-2 home win over Crystal Palace, but Frank Lampard's main striker Taiwo Awoniyi went off with an ankle injury in that game; there is still no diagnosis, and Sidiki Cherif or Ellis Simms are the likely stand-ins. The numbers already treat Awoniyi as out (about -10% on Coventry's goals), along with Woolfenden, Amenda and Eccles, so my earlier small cut for him would now count him twice and is removed. Caleb Yirenkyi and Ephron Mason-Clark are listed as doubts. Paul Tierney referees; his slightly low card record is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals: 1.8 for Leeds and 0.9 for Coventry. Leeds' attack is sharp after four goals at Chelsea, and Coventry have conceded 11 in six, but that form is already counted. Awoniyi's ankle injury is also already in the numbers (about -10% on Coventry's goals), so I no longer take anything extra off and stay at about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers expect 8.3 corners: 5.2 for Leeds and 3.2 for Coventry. They already lower both sides for recent form, especially Coventry, who have won few corners lately. Leeds attack with wide play and crosses, which fits the home side winning most of them, and the team news changes nothing here, so I stay at about 8.3.

cards.text: The numbers expect 2.7 cards, with Coventry slightly more likely to be booked as the away side. They already count Leeds picking up more cards than usual lately, Coventry fewer, and Paul Tierney's slightly low card rate (3.8 a game). It is not a derby and there are no bans in play, so I stay at about 2.7.

shots.text: The numbers expect 28.1 shots, 18.5 of them from Leeds at home, which already includes Leeds shooting more than usual in their last six games. Okafor and Calvert-Lewin are both fit, which matches that picture. Coventry may be without Awoniyi, but the numbers already assume that, so I stay at about 28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers expect 8.4 shots on target: 5.2 for Leeds and 3.2 for Coventry. Leeds' sharper recent finishing is already counted, and so is Coventry's loss of Awoniyi up front. With Cherif or Simms the likely replacement and nothing else new, I stay at about 8.4.
